Queue build [31509278524](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/31509278524) is red on `packages/spec/src/data/api-methods-batch-conformance.test.ts` › *grants bulk wherever it grants create / update / delete*. **Not this PR, and not flaky — it fails identically on the base branch.** This is triage-checklist case 2, already owned by **#7793**; ⛔ **do not re-queue this PR until that lands** — a re-queue just burns another full-suite rebuild for everything behind it.

**Reproduced independently, not inferred** — same test run in two worktrees:

- on this branch (`233052da`) → 1 failed | 3 passed
- on **`origin/main` @ `098b62914`**, my base, with my changes absent → **1 failed | 3 passed**, byte-identical offender:

```
sys_api_key: [get, list, update] grants single-record writes but not 'bulk' —
/batch and the *Many routes will 405 (packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts)
```

**Why it cannot be mine:** this PR's diff against `origin/main` restricted to `packages/` is **empty** — it touches `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` and one `.changeset/` file, nothing else. The failing test file-scans `*.object.ts` sources under `packages/` and reads neither `scripts/` nor `.changeset/`, so there is no path by which this diff reaches it. The named file was last touched by `52200b43d` (#7769), which is an ancestor of my base.

That matches #7793's recorded mechanism exactly (#7769 opened `update` on `sys_api_key` without `bulk` or a `SINGLE_RECORD_WRITE_ONLY` entry; PR-side affected-subset CI cannot see a `packages/spec` file-scan test for a `platform-objects` diff, so only full-suite queue builds go red). I am not fixing it here: it is another seat's dispatched issue and `packages/platform-objects` / the conformance test are outside this PR's scope.

This PR's own gates are green — `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` (self-test 153 assertions), ESLint, TypeScript, Check Changeset, Test Core — and all 20 PR-side check runs passed or were path-skipped. Happy to re-queue once #7793 lands; I'll act on the base-recovered signal rather than polling.

**Kick receipt — foreign failure, ⛔ deliberately NOT re-queued.**

PR #7805 was in the merge queue (`gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-7805-fa341b1f`) at 16:22Z and was **kicked** by 16:51Z. Classified by the ruled criteria (#7492 / #7518), not by guesswork:

| signature | reading |
|---|---|
| landed? | ⛔ no — `state: open`, `merged: false`, main still at `098b62914` ~10 min later. Not the *`removed_from_merge_queue` + `merged` within ~1s* shape. |
| queue-rebuild collateral (no `merge_group` run at all)? | ⛔ no — this PR had **5** `merge_group` runs of its own |
| which run failed | `CI` (run `31512043909`), jobs `Test Core (1/3)` and the `Test Core` roster leg |

**The failure is foreign, proven by content:**

```
FAIL src/data/api-methods-batch-conformance.test.ts
  > apiMethods conformance — single-record writes imply batch (#3026)
+ "sys_api_key: [get, list, update] grants single-record writes but not 'bulk'
   (packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts)"
```

This PR's entire diff is `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` + one changeset — **2 files, nothing in `platform-objects`, nothing in `packages/spec/src`**. It cannot produce a `sys_api_key` apiMethods conformance failure.

The offender is **already on `main`** (`52200b43d`, PR #7769 / #7727) and is escalated as **#7824**.

## ⛔ Why no re-queue

The protocol allows one re-queue with a receipt when the signature is foreign. **It is deliberately not being used here**, because the defect is on the **base**, not in the batch composition — a re-queue would rebuild the merge group on the same red `main` and be kicked by the identical assertion. That is not a retry, it is a loop.

⇒ **Held for base recovery.** Auto-merge stays armed; when #7824 lands, this PR re-enters the queue on a green base. If it is kicked a *second* time after the base is green, it goes to the queue steward (#5810), not back through me.

## The delivery itself is unaffected and was accepted on review

Worth restating, since a kick can read as doubt about the work: the report's method was the strongest kind. It **rejected its own first fix by its own positive control** — the wider "any line-final letter governs" predicate turned every label wrapped under an ordinary sentence into a mention, precisely the failure #7078 predicted when it declined to attempt this — and pinned that rejection as fixture **P52** rather than merely describing it.

Both halves of the two-sided bar were measured on the whole v17 stock (unshallowed): branch-1 hits 176 → 174, **`--audit-stock` output byte-identical before and after** (residue 97, `!` candidates 52, unchanged), and **exactly two state changes, both named and both verified mentions on inspection** — including confirmation that `tidy-donkeys-yawn`, the measured false positive of a *different* mechanism, is untouched. Self-test 142 → 153 assertions, pinning both directions. One limitation stated rather than hidden: prose wrapped *inside* a fenced block gets one line of context, not block structure; no stock occurrence has that shape.
